title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 14: Oracle Tumbles on Hotter CPI Data Lifting Treasury Yields
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: Oracle stock fell 8.83% on October 14, 2026, following hotter-than-expected September CPI data that lifted Treasury yields and revived rate-hike concerns. The decline was compounded by existing worries about Oracle's AI cloud expansion costs, including Project Jupiter data center spending, which has pushed debt toward $167 billion and resulted in a credit rating downgrade to BBB-. Despite strong 30% year-over-year revenue growth driven by triple-digit cloud infrastructure gains, investors are concerned about margin pressure and the company's shrinking free cash flow, with potential dividend cuts possible.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock declined 8.83% due to elevated inflation concerns triggering rate-hike bets, combined with mounting debt ($167 billion), credit rating downgrade to BBB-, shrinking free cash flow, and potential dividend cuts. While cloud revenue growth is strong at 30% YoY, heavy AI infrastructure spending and execution risks outweigh positive momentum.

title: Salesforce vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Pamela Kock
description: Salesforce and Palantir are compared as AI-integrated enterprise software leaders. Salesforce offers mature, steady cash flow ($14.4B free cash flow) with conservative valuation (13.7x forward P/E), while Palantir demonstrates explosive 56% revenue growth but trades at a premium valuation (130.8x forward P/E) with customer concentration risk. The article recommends Salesforce for most investors seeking a better risk-reward balance, though Palantir offers higher upside potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Established market leader with strong fundamentals: $41.5B revenue (9.6% YoY growth), $14.4B free cash flow, 18% net margin, conservative 0.3x debt-to-equity ratio, and attractive 13.7x forward P/E valuation. Successfully integrating AI through Agentforce platform with diversified customer base.

Demonstrates impressive 56% revenue growth and 36.3% net margin with strong AI Platform adoption, but carries significant risks: extremely high 130.8x forward P/E valuation, customer concentration (top 3 clients = 16% revenue), reliance on third-party cloud providers, and ethical scrutiny. Higher risk-reward profile suitable only for growth-focused investors.

title: Salesforce vs. ServiceNow: Which AI Software Stock Has the Edge?
author: Na
description: Salesforce and ServiceNow are both expanding their AI capabilities, but Salesforce emerges as the more attractive investment. Salesforce's Agentforce ARR surged 240% YoY to $1.5B with rising earnings estimates, while trading at a forward P/E of 14.76 versus ServiceNow's 28.99. ServiceNow shows strong AI adoption but faces margin pressure from higher infrastructure costs and acquisition-related financial risks.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Rapid AI growth with Agentforce ARR up 240% YoY to $1.5B, upward earnings estimate revisions (18% increase over 60 days), lower forward P/E valuation of 14.76, and successful conversion of large customer base to AI products.

Strong AI ACV growth exceeding $1B with 40% sequential acceleration and 9x increase in Agentic AI production customers, but offset by declining gross margins (78% vs 81% YoY), higher AI infrastructure costs, flat earnings estimates over 60 days, and elevated valuation at 28.99 forward P/E with acquisition-related financial risks.

title: Intuit vs. Oracle: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: John Ballard
description: The article compares Intuit and Oracle as investment options in 2026. Intuit trades at cheaper valuations but faces intense competition from low-cost alternatives and fintech startups in the tax software space. Oracle shows stronger growth momentum with 30% year-over-year cloud revenue growth and a large backlog of contracted services, though it carries higher debt levels. The author recommends Oracle over Intuit, citing Oracle's positioning in the growing AI infrastructure market versus Intuit's vulnerability to competitive moat erosion.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Intuit shows solid financial metrics (77.91% gross margin, 21% net margin, $21B revenue with 14% growth), it faces significant headwinds from competition in tax software and uncertainty about customer retention. The cheaper valuation is viewed as a potential value trap rather than an opportunity.

Oracle demonstrates accelerating revenue growth (17% YoY, 30% cloud growth), strong operating cash flow ($47B trailing-12-month), improving leverage (debt-to-equity fell from 3.6x to 2.3x), and strategic positioning in the high-demand AI infrastructure market. The author explicitly recommends Oracle as the better investment choice.

title: C3.ai vs. UiPath: Which AI-Driven Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares C3.ai and UiPath as investments in the agentic AI automation space. UiPath is recommended as the better buy due to its profitability, positive free cash flow, and consistent growth trajectory. C3.ai, while showing recent improvements like positive free cash flow and 73% quarter-over-quarter booking growth, remains unprofitable with substantial net losses and is still in early restructuring stages under CEO Thomas Siebel.

Not recommended for investment at this time.
